body.title: WSL transcript filesystem result, deadline and process ownership
body.result: Actual child operations return access:true, stat/lstat native Stats, readdir projected entries, readfile native string/Buffer, open monotonic numeric handle, read Buffer sliced to bytesRead, close:true even missing handle after deleting its map entry. IPC decoder restores Stats prototype and Dirent functions, otherwise returns raw value; it does not validate every schema. Parent exposes frozen opaque process-owned handle, maps ownership in WeakMaps, returns bytesRead from decoded body and close void. Unknown operation falls through undefined in child; request correlation is by active id. No subprocess, filesystem request or WSL operation was executed.
body.stateTransitionsAndEffects: Gate permits2 tasks, at most1 scan, one per lane; exact priority precedes scan. Queue/waiter bounds64 each, exact deadline30s/scan60s, dedupe only byte-identical operation+path+priority except open/read intentionally undeduped. Caller abort removes waiter; running I/O keeps permit until settlement/deadline, with abandoned resource disposal. Task deadline aborts process, quarantines route and rejects queued route tasks unavailable. Backoff starts5s, doubles up to2*deadline, shared incident does not escalate and strikes decay after5min; real timely filesystem result can clear quarantine, late result or transport fault cannot.
body.errorAndPartialSuccess: One child per lane, one active request, close prioritized ahead of later work; close deadline30s and idle reap60s. Abort/send error/disconnect/exit rejects active request and retires slot, marks handles faulted, attempts SIGKILL without claiming process death. Missing/faulted handle is classified failure; unknown close is idempotent. Child close deletes handle before native close, so rejection can follow ownership retirement. Open racing child exit refuses handle publication. Corrupt decodable-response failure retires slot, late nonmatching ids ignored; message shape itself is not comprehensively validated. Child serializes name/message plus typed errno/code/syscall/path, send failure is swallowed on dying channel. Access helper native close can override read outcome; process-owned close errors are deliberately swallowed/fire-and-forget. Vitest in-process route requires BOTH VITEST=true and worker global, so those tests alone cannot prove production IPC.
body.externalBoundary: Source chain now reaches actual node:fs/promises and node:child_process.fork/send/kill. Fork uses staged/unpacked entry discovery, allowlisted environment with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, empty execArgv, advanced serialization and hidden Windows child; missing entry rejects. Packaging/env allowlist remains inherited E5 configuration obligation, not a fabricated model/service result.

methods.resultContract: {ok:true,viewer} | {ok:false,error}; connects, verifies /myself (api/3 cloud or api/2 server), stores token, writes site file, returns viewer. Shared HTTP body returns null on204, otherwise parsed JSON, non-OK throws JiraApiError(status) from joined messages/errors/message or status fallback; no token deletion inside HTTP helper. Node default is actual global fetch with null proxy session; injected desktop client owns Chromium behavior. Attachment requests initially require exact configured origin; redirect behavior remains provider/native and must be tested. Lead: token write uses injected SecretStore encryption when available or mode0600 plaintext fallback; token cache updated only after write. Site catalog cache changes before mode0600 direct write, so disk failure can leave memory ahead; empty/malformed catalog reads normalize empty. Token deletion clears memory and ignores unlink failure, so disk residue can survive. Credential decryption errors are recorded/rethrown, other token read errors become null. Lead identity body: URL adds https only if no scheme, trims trailing path slashes and removes query/hash; it does not enforce an HTTP-only scheme. Site ID is first24 base64url SHA256 of normalized URL, newline, lowercased email or verified PAT accountId. Viewer accountId falls back cloud accountId->server name->key->empty, display/email to fallback, avatar48->32->undefined. Token write precedes catalog write so latter failure leaves token; catalog cache may already advance. SecretStore is global Symbol.for slot and missing startup installation throws, caught as connection failure. Desktop binding installed at preflight225 forwards Electron.safeStorage; plain-Node orcad installs unavailable encryption (encrypt/decryptthrow), so Jira's own fallback writes plaintext when unavailable. Linux basic_text is still encryptionAvailable but reports protection gap; native crypto error semantics stay native boundary. No credential/environment value was accessed in this audit.

Workspace path derivation honors trimmed repo override then global root, selects win32 path operations for Windows-like paths, nests by repo basename without .git only when configured. leadRunnerReuse.contract: gh/glab runner result succeeds only exit0 without timeout/truncation/aborted signal; otherwise throws enriched code/killed/signal/stdout/stderr. Termination-barrier runProcess uses accepted E4-F07 native process contract; clipped output is error, never usable shorter JSON. gh retries only recognized idempotent read failures,3attempts with250/1000ms delays, no mutation retry; glab no analogous retry. Host/WSL selection remains separate exact scope obligation. GH host args pin api --hostname only if absent and qualify --repo/-R/--repo= owner/repo even for github.com; already qualified or URL passes through, combined short -R forms untouched. On Windows cwd WSL wins over override; translate UNC and drive args, explicit distro cwd runs there, command args shell-quoted, native spawn cwd revalidated outside deletable workspace. Missing WSL gh can fall back to native only with explicit repository/API context (no API placeholders), auth or explicit repo-view target; host ENOENT can try default distro. SSH alias resolution uses ssh -G -- host in the repository host/WSL scope with5s budget; success60s/failure5s TTL,256cap and singleflight with provider generation. Failed alias is indeterminate, not negative identity. URL identity accepts exactly owner/repo for allowed schemes, strips .git; HTTP ports retained but SSH/git transport ports ignored; ssh.github.com folds to github.com. Native ssh-G uses HOME-specific -F only when existing home config differs from passwd home; native runProcess failure/nonzero/timeout gives null. Remote URL probe30s with owner-provider absence null; only no-such-remote is stable missing, transport/abort never negative cache. Git-config signatures inspect common/worktree config and includes;2s caller deadline yields undefined without canceling underlying read; shared probe is replaceable after60s and late ownership token cannot overwrite successor. WSL captured login uses getent preferred executable shell, SHELL/bash then sh fallback, bash/zsh/ksh interactive login, unsupported shell sh; output last nonce begin fence and first end, missing begin=>null, missingend leaves remainder including exit hooks. Process group wrapper probes setsid --wait, otherwise no group identity; random stderr marker parses only safe PGID>1,512tail. TERM/KILL each checks kill-0 up to40x25ms under5s subprocess bound; unknown PGID=>false, native root exit alone not guest deathproof. General runWslProcess uses one budget including optional environment probe, no login fallback after degraded probe, validates absolute guestcwd and argv, longscript goes stdin; result code/stdout/stderr/timedOut/environmentResolved omits lower-level truncation fields. Guest environment success cached untilinvalidate; absent executable10min/otherfailure5s, bounded shared probe and generation fence prevent latecacheoverwrite.
leadRunnerReuse.limitation: E4-F07 native process result reused; gh/glab/SSH/WSL runtime/provider effects and cross-version/platform execution remain unrun. Missing identity or contact remains unverifiable.

Lead-reviewed supplement: Excerpt mode only changes ok:true results: keep final 512K characters before ANSI/section stripping and CR normalization, then preserve recent 100 lines plus at most 30 earlier error-context lines (or last 200 lines), capped to 16KiB UTF-8; trim final result. Failure union passes through. UTF-8 cap walks complete codepoints backwards, lone surrogates 3 bytes; nonpositive budget empty. ANSI strip removes complete OSC/string/CSI/escape sequences, not separately exported generic control-character regex.

remainingExecutionTests: server PAT vs Basic; PAT id collision; token persistence
reviewedLeafMethods.resultContract: {ok:true,viewer} | {ok:false,error}; connects, verifies /myself (api/3 cloud or api/2 server), stores token, writes site file, returns viewer. Shared HTTP body returns null on204, otherwise parsed JSON, non-OK throws JiraApiError(status) from joined messages/errors/message or status fallback; no token deletion inside HTTP helper. Node default is actual global fetch with null proxy session; injected desktop client owns Chromium behavior. Attachment requests initially require exact configured origin; redirect behavior remains provider/native and must be tested. Lead: token write uses injected SecretStore encryption when available or mode0600 plaintext fallback; token cache updated only after write. Site catalog cache changes before mode0600 direct write, so disk failure can leave memory ahead; empty/malformed catalog reads normalize empty. Token deletion clears memory and ignores unlink failure, so disk residue can survive. Credential decryption errors are recorded/rethrown, other token read errors become null. Lead identity body: URL adds https only if no scheme, trims trailing path slashes and removes query/hash; it does not enforce an HTTP-only scheme. Site ID is first24 base64url SHA256 of normalized URL, newline, lowercased email or verified PAT accountId. Viewer accountId falls back cloud accountId->server name->key->empty, display/email to fallback, avatar48->32->undefined. Token write precedes catalog write so latter failure leaves token; catalog cache may already advance. SecretStore is global Symbol.for slot and missing startup installation throws, caught as connection failure. Desktop binding installed at preflight225 forwards Electron.safeStorage; plain-Node orcad installs unavailable encryption (encrypt/decryptthrow), so Jira's own fallback writes plaintext when unavailable. Linux basic_text is still encryptionAvailable but reports protection gap; native crypto error semantics stay native boundary. No credential/environment value was accessed in this audit.

contract.title: Execution host identity, scope and ownership
behavior: parseExecutionHostId trims outer input, recognizes exact local or ssh:/runtime: with nonempty encoded suffix, rejects raw pipe and malformed percent escapes, and requires a nonempty decoded suffix. It preserves original encoded suffix spelling in id; to* constructors encodeURIComponent the trimmed target.

normalizeExecutionHostScope maps absent/blank/all/invalid to all; requestedExecutionHostScope first substitutes local only for nullish input. Therefore omission is local but explicit empty/invalid is all. Visible arrays drop malformed entries and duplicates in order; no valid entries =>null; order normalization uses [] instead.

Repo ownership prefers valid explicit host then legacy connection then local. getRepoSshConnectionId answers where files live: runtime host can retain nested legacy SSH; explicit local suppresses contradictory SSH. getSshTargetIdForExecutionHost answers what this caller can dial and returns a target only for ssh:. Worktree hostId nullishly wins without revalidation, then populated repo ownership, then provided default.

Focused environment maps to runtime:<encoded-id> or local. Labels use explicit platform or navigator Windows/Mac/Linux/X11 before process.platform; local labels Mac/Windows/Linux/This computer. Invalid ids label Unknown host, all labels All hosts; remote labels use decoded id. runtime-ssh- is a discriminator, not a distinct host namespace.

contract.title: Key grammar, Linear bounds and exact agent enum
behavior: Hotkey splits + and trims, requires >=2 nonempty parts and exactly one nonmodifier; matching lowercases and removes whitespace/_/-. Modifier set is alt,cmd,cmdorctrl,command,commandorcontrol,control,ctrl,meta,option,shift,super,win. Duplicate modifiers and unknown single base-key names are allowed. No normalized key string is returned; success is null and original CLI value is forwarded.

Press-key requires trimmed nonempty single key; literal + is allowed, any other plus-bearing string rejects. Click-modifiers require 1..4 nonempty modifier tokens, case-fold only, with duplicate modifiers allowed; interior separators/whitespace aliases accepted by hotkey are not accepted here. Failures are stable validation hint strings, mapped by S1 handlers to invalid_argument.

Linear search undefined/nonfinite defaults20; otherwise floor and clamp1..50. Depth undefined/nonfinite defaults2; otherwise floor/clamp0..5. Direct null/non-number values fail Number.isFinite and default; CLI numeric parser remains the outer contract. Caps/constants and TypeScript request/error unions in agent-access are declarations, not additional runtime validation. UUID accepts case-insensitive hex8-4-4-4-12 without version/variant enforcement.

isTuiAgent requires typeof string and Object.hasOwn(TUI_AGENT_CONFIG,value), with no trim/case/alias normalization. Exact keys: claude, claude-agent-teams, openclaude, codex, autohand, ante, trae, opencode, mimo-code, pi, omp, prime-agent, gemini, antigravity, aider, goose, amp, kilo, kiro, crush, aug, cline, codebuff, command-code, continue, cursor, droid, kimi, mistral-vibe, qwen-code, rovo, hermes, openclaw, copilot, grok, devin. Detect aliases are not enum aliases.

Disabled-agent normalization accepts arrays only, filters by isTuiAgent and deduplicates preserving order. Auto-pick returns null for blank preference, otherwise preferred if detected+enabled then explicit catalog priority, else null. These helpers do not establish provider installation or authenticate selected model.
remainingTests: Port computer-use-key-spec.test.ts and relevant Linear/automation CLI assertions from S1; add duplicate modifiers, unknown base key, normalization asymmetry, null/NaN/infinity/fraction clamp cases, UUID invalid hex/shape versus valid nonstandard version, and enum prototype/case/alias rejection.

contract.owner: Calling filesystem host; path functions own fd, handle overload leaves caller fd open
contract.contract: Sync validates max nonnegative safe integer before open; async path opens first then handle variant validates inside try/finally. fstat/stat size must safe integer>=0 and <=max; no regular-file/symlink/ownership guard. Allocates initial size, positioned reads until EOF, returning truncated-to-read buffer and ORIGINAL stats; handles shrink. Once full probes1 byte, rejects if offset>=max otherwise grows at least64KiB/double but <=max, copies probe, repeats to capture growth. Exact max at EOF succeeds, max+1 rejects NodeFileReadTooLargeError(observed,max), max0 admits empty only. Path wrappers always close; close failure can replace prior success/error. OS allocation/read/stat exceptions propagate, giant safe limits can still allocation-fail.
tests: Port node-bounded-file-reader.test.ts; exact/max0/growth/shrink/sparse/short reads and initial invalid size, async-open-before-validation versus sync-validation-before-open, directory/symlink/read/close errors and original stats after growth.

contract.owner: Process runs on invoking execution host; caller owns streams for spawnProcess; barrier is local process-tree observation, never remote ownership proof
contract.contract:
resolveSpawn always shell:false/windowsHide:true, default pipe streams, caller env/cwd/detached/verbatim; barrier forces detached on POSIX. Windows .cmd/.bat uses spec.env.ComSpec ?? process.env.ComSpec ?? cmd.exe and a single verbatim /d /v:off /s /c command line; quotes/backslashes/percent escaped, CR/LF rejected. This differs from stricter CLI windows-batch-spawn rejection helper.
Async run pre-abort invokes termination callback and returns code/signal null, empty streams,timedOut false without spawning. Default30s and8MiB per stream; timeout null disables, no safe-delay guard here. Input ends stdin immediately; stream errors swallowed, stdout/stderr capture PREFIX bytes with possible replacement char at UTF-8 cutoff and outputTruncated true. Nonzero exit resolves, spawn/child errors reject; settle clears timers/abort listener. Nonbarrier timeout/abort signals root then SIGKILL after2s and resolves even without close.
Barrier signals tree, defers error/exit/close; Windows initial verified result can settle early, POSIX waits force verification after2s; failed attempts kill root and set a10s deadline before settling unverified. Root exit before stopping can permit settlement; close invokes exactly-once reporter. Returned ProcessResult omits barrier verification, so null result or cancellation is NOT tree exit proof; reporting callback can throw. POSIX tree signals negative pid, force probes ps pgid/state up to2s treating all zombies as quiescent; fallback kill0 only ESRCH proves absent (EPERM remains exists). Windows skips taskkill if real exit/signal known to avoid recycled PID; taskkill /t /f close0 counts success, error/nonzero/2s timeout falls back root and false. OS races/actual descendant proof remain integration obligations.
Sync variant uses same argv with spawnSync timeout/maxBuffer and buffer decoding; ETIMEDOUT becomes timedOut true, other errors including ENOBUFS throw, outputTruncated always false. It does not implement async abort/barrier/callback behavior despite accepting the same spec. Kill observer is optional diagnostic, exceptions ignored.
The10s unverified deadline starts only after barrier signal/force promises resolve and mark the attempt complete; a supplied barrier Promise that never settles can prevent that deadline from starting. This contradicts any unconditional bounded-settlement interpretation and needs a dedicated regression.
tests: Port run-process, Windows command-line, bounded-output and process-tree assertions; exercise timeout/abort before/after spawn, stream EPIPE, prefix truncation, descendant pipe retention, custom barrier rejecting/hanging/false, deadline with no root exit and reporter exactly-once.

Actual isolated POSIX/Windows child trees, zombie/permission/recycled PID protections; demonstrate unverified result cannot release shared-resource ownership. Sync ETIMEDOUT/ENOBUFS/no signal handling and adversarial .cmd argv corpus on Windows.

contract.title: trustedOrcaHooks prompt, persistence and callers
body: ensureHooksConfirmed serializes modal work with a promise queue whose rejected predecessor does not poison the next prompt. Setup trust hashes trimmed setup plus indexed/labeled defaultTabs commands; VM recipe trust includes lifecycle declarations and identity/display fields. Repository-wide trust can bypass content inspection; duplicate repo IDs disable that wide bypass. Per-script trust remains keyed by repoId/script kind/content hash, with runtime or SSH owner selection supplied separately by the caller. Local-only and local issue-command paths bypass shared trust; shared inspection failure fails closed to skip.

Cancellation is checked before inspection/hash and before displaying a prompt; an already displayed modal has no general AbortSignal cancellation loop in this helper. The modal settles once, dismissal means skip, and always-trust state is reset on open. Run optionally records trust before resolving. UI trust actions clone/replace the map optimistically and fire window.api.ui.set with logging on rejection: they neither await durable save nor roll back the displayed trust state.

Desktop ui:set ignores the event identity at this handler and forwards typed partial updates to the profile store; this is not the stricter Skills IPC sender gate. Paired ui.set validates the strict outer schema but trustedOrcaHooks is only record<string,unknown>. It removes pairing-local fields; trustedOrcaHooks is not among those exclusions. Runtime updateUIState calls store update then immediately reads state. Persisted UI merges general durable updates, schedules saving and notifies; a trust map is replaced as a field, not transactionally merged across writers. E2 owns the accepted SP01–SP13 durable writer contract beyond this scheduling boundary.

Hydration rejects dangerous top-level keys/non-record values but does not validate every nested trust record. With no valid repo IDs yet, sanitized trust survives the pending catalog. Only a latest-generation successful all-host load prunes unknown repo IDs; local-first, remote failure and stale completion must preserve remote entries. Pruning updates renderer state and does not itself write the pruned map durably.

Full/quick composer preparation passes host/runtime identity and cancellation checks; skip can suppress setup and issue-command launch, and quick ask-policy can defer to the advanced UI. VM creation gates recipe launch on trust. Automation saves a skipped setup decision when trust is declined. Direct work-item launch calls ensureHooksConfirmed without the explicit host parameter used by composer, so duplicate-ID routing needs a discriminating test. Removal bypasses archive trust for forget-local and otherwise checks owner/generation after awaiting confirmation. These are caller-level contracts, not a claim that every subsequent creator, archive writer or provider operation is atomic.
contract.boundary: E2 accepted settings/persistence/shortcut source gate; WP-ENG-WORKTREES and E1 own full composer/archive execution; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns host routing. Retain nested malformed map behavior, optimistic-save failures and concurrent whole-map updates as explicit acceptance obligations.
tests: same repo ID on two hosts with different content; repo-wide versus script trust isolation; UI save rejection then restart; concurrent edits do not silently erase trust; malicious nested values/prototype keys; all-host partial/failure/generation race; cancellation before/while modal; exact approved content versus target-branch changed hooks; paired-mobile trust write permissions

contract.title: Setup environment and defaultTabs consumption
body: Setup environment provides four compatibility root/worktree path variables, workspace name, and the internal Git credential guard policy. Local runtime obtains effective created-worktree hooks, translates runHooks/setupDecision, and obtains defaultTabs separately. A default-tabs decision failure keeps templates with runCommands false; setup decision failures have different caller catches. Runner generation failure can return a successfully created worktree without launch, and the non-runner path can start a background hook through an imported runner with logged unsuccessful results.

Runner files live under git rev-parse --git-path per-worktree metadata. WSL paths map to UNC for Node filesystem writes. Script write is direct, not an atomic rename. Native Windows chooses cmd unless a usable POSIX shell and a shebang demand POSIX; interpreter choice and terminal launch shell are separate. Git Bash converts only the four path keys; the WSL loop applies Linux path conversion to all environment values, despite the narrower comment. POSIX mode is 0755 where supported. Wait behavior ORs local and project policy.

Runtime creates default tabs before setup, honors runCommands for trimmed template commands, and applies titles/colors. Each failed tab can leave preceding tabs; a color failure can leave an already collected handle. Setup uses split/new-tab policy, may create a primary fallback tab, and optionally observes completion with a UUID token/env. A returned PTY ID is needed to record observation. The outer catch allows partial state; there is no universal rollback.

Renderer application marks defaults applied before creating tabs, so failed creation does not automatically retry. First-tab startup command can override the first default command; remaining commands respect runCommands. Titles/colors, activation and queued setup/issue commands go through renderer-owned execution queues. This is distinct from main runtime provisioning and not proof both paths are deduplicated under reconnection.

Remote worktree setup reads the created tree's YAML through remote providers, creates the remote runner under remote Git metadata and chooses script format from the remote absolute path. Local-only shared/symlink/include behavior is explicitly separated in source. The local IPC path likewise reads created YAML and only writes the runner rather than invisibly executing it; runner failure after Git creation degrades to created-without-setup. Reuse accepted effective-hook parsing and policy helpers; preserve the mismatch possibility between trust inspected before creation and effective target-tree content.
contract.boundary: WP-ENG-WORKTREES owns Git creation/provisioning and effective-hook decisions; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns fs/Git provider semantics; WP-ENG-TERMINAL/E1 own actual shell execution, command queues and completion. Imported script-text/parser/provider internals are explicit boundaries.
tests: run/skip/inherit/ask across CLI, desktop and SSH; defaultTabs no-command/title-only and denied commands; setup failure after committed Git create; partial tab/color failure and reconnect dedup; WSL value conversion versus Git Bash paths; Windows cmd/POSIX shebang/native shell; completion token with missing/late PTY; approved content drift

contract.title: Relay handler admission and cancellation retirement
body: Reuse the independent relay review's method lists, not the weaker leaf. Service wiring constructs shared PTY/fs/Git stream/watch contexts and registers preflight, skills, external automation, ports, agent execution and workspace session methods. AiVault initialization can throw; only explicit unsupported/absent cases are soft. Plugin identity absence degrades availability. Remote proxy routes exclude the origin and use per-method timeout. Session-root truthiness/casts and home expansion here are not auth/containment checks.

Dispatcher creates a client session identity, defaulting to unproved/unauthenticated. Request routing attaches identity, generation-stale predicate, AbortSignal and response-settlement callbacks to handlers; it does not universally enforce their permissions. Missing method is -32601; selected numeric errors survive, others become -32000; only specific structured error schemas are forwarded. rpc.cancel aborts the same client's request. Notification handlers have a different no-await path. A handler must enforce its own authenticated owner capabilities and validate parameters.

PTY open adapts several values coercively with Number/String and accepts optional objects without deep schema; requiring a session identity is not requiring authenticated=true. Reconnect transport delegates handshake verification, attaches credential/version-derived identity, backpressure and leftover data, and detaches on peer close. Loss of attachment is not a PTY exit verdict. Preserve Git 2.25 and both wire-version directions at downstream Git/fs/PTY handlers.

deliveryCanceled retirement is fenced by mux/token/client generation/owner generation/incarnation. Recovery-pending branches restore and wake. In the normal branch applySshPtySourceCancellationProof returns a boolean, including false if no installed intake, but the caller ignores it and then retires/deletes delivery state. Throws preserve a different outcome. This confirms the independent review's exact unanswered result-handling issue; it does not prove a live failure. The distinct recovery-proof branch must not be conflated with this one.

Owned-process disposal awaits skills then best-effort AiVault; handler disposal calls fs/Git cleanup with no universal catch. No broad claim that all registrations, subprocesses or watches have completed teardown is justified.
contract.boundary: WP-ENG-RELAY owns dispatcher and concrete registered handlers; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns SSH identity/intake; Git/fs/PTY handlers and third-party adapters remain named implementation boundaries, not permission inherited from registration. E3 owns runtime schema/receiver linkage.
